founded.what: The year the house dates itself from, when a family of Vertus and a wine trading family of Villers-Franqueux joined their businesses, by the house and the union.

kind.means: A négociant manipulant, a house in the trade's own word: it farms its own vines, buys grapes beyond them and makes the wine itself, and the Union des Maisons de Champagne lists it among the houses.

story: Duval-Leroy was born of two small wine businesses. By the chronology of the Union des Maisons de Champagne, in 1857 a Duval of Vertus and a Leroy, a wine trader of Villers-Franqueux, agreed to join their businesses, and the house dates itself from 1859, the year it took the joined name at Vertus, in the south of the Côte des Blancs. The founding families ran it through the generations that followed. The great turn came at the end of the twentieth century. The 1990 vintage gave the first Femme de Champagne, a prestige cuvée of Grand Cru Chardonnay, by two accounts. In 1991 the head of the house died, and his widow, who had married into the founding family, took the presidency that year. The house turned early to greener farming: by its own account it made the first certified organic Brut of a Champagne house, and it says it was the first house farming sustainably to win the High Environmental Value certificate. It owns vines around Vertus, among them the Clos des Bouveries at Vertus, and buys grapes beyond them.

style.line: Fresh and precise, shaped by the Chardonnay of the Côte des Blancs where the house stands, with the Pinot Noir of the Montagne de Reims for body in the classic range.
style.grapes: Chardonnay from the Côte des Blancs around Vertus leads the prestige wines; Brut Réserve is Pinot Noir led, with Meunier and a little Chardonnay, from about fifteen crus by the house.
style.reserve: Brut Réserve holds at least two fifths reserve wine, by the house's technical sheet.
style.malolactic: Brut Réserve goes through its malolactic conversion, by the house's technical sheet.
style.lees: Brut Réserve ages 30 to 36 months on its lees, by the house's technical sheet.
style.dosage: Brut Réserve is dosed at 8 grams a litre, by the house's technical sheet.

nv.name: Brut Réserve
nv.note: The non vintage Brut: Pinot Noir led, with Meunier and a little Chardonnay, at least two fifths reserve wine, three years or so on its lees.

cuvee.name: Femme de Champagne

first.what: The first vintage, by two accounts; when it was first released differs between sources, so no release year is given.

cuvee.rhythm: Made only in vintages the house judges exceptional, since the 1990. Its own pages show the 2000, 2002 and 2004, and critics have tasted the 1996 and the 2008.
cuvee.blend: Chardonnay leads by far, Grand Cru from the Côte des Blancs, with a little Grand Cru Pinot Noir; the share has moved by vintage, by the house's pages.
cuvee.sites: Grand Cru villages: for the 2002, Chardonnay from Avize, Cramant, Oger and Le Mesnil-sur-Oger and Pinot Noir from Ambonnay, by the house; later vintages drew Pinot Noir from the Montagne de Reims.
cuvee.making: The base wines of each village are made apart, and a part of them is fermented in oak barrels, the share moving by vintage, about a fifth of the 2002 in barrels of 220 litres by the house's sheet, and by critics' notes on the 2000, 2004 and 2008. The 2002 was bottled as a Brut Nature, with no sugar added at disgorging, by the house's page. Other vintages carry a light dosage that the pages read do not give.
cuvee.lees: Long: the house's pages read give no figure, and one tasting note says the 2006 reached the market after sixteen years.
cuvee.young: Ripe hazelnut and honeysuckle, then candied mandarin peel, with a fine, lacy texture, by the house's own note on one vintage and a critic's on another.
cuvee.aged: Slow to show its years: one critic found the 2008 only on the cusp of development, and another a buttery thread through a long, fresh finish.

forms.name: Femme de Champagne Rosé
forms.note: A vintage rosé of Grand Cru Pinot Noir alone, by the house's page for the 2007; the 2008 was made by saignée.

forms.name: Femme de Champagne Grand Cru Brut
forms.note: A non vintage form of the same Grand Cru wine, made beside the vintage.

cuvee.serve: 9 to 11 degrees Celsius, never ice cold; no need to decant; a tulip or a white wine glass, where the oak and the Chardonnay can open.

table.house45: Duval-Leroy is a family house of Vertus, in the south of the Côte des Blancs, founded in 1859 when two wine families joined their businesses. It grew as a family business, generation after generation. After the head of the house died in 1991, his widow took the lead, and the house turned towards greener farming. By its own account it made the first certified organic Brut of a Champagne house. Its Chardonnay country gives a fresh, precise style. Most guests know Brut Réserve, and the prestige cuvée is Femme de Champagne.
table.house10: Duval-Leroy is the family house of Vertus in the Côte des Blancs, founded in 1859 and known for its Chardonnay and its green farming.
table.cuvee45: Femme de Champagne is the vintage prestige cuvée of Duval-Leroy, first made in 1990. It is mostly Chardonnay from the Grand Cru villages of the Côte des Blancs, with a little Pinot Noir from Ambonnay. A part of the wine is fermented in oak, and it rests for many years before release. The house is in the Côte des Blancs, so the Chardonnay is its own country. Expect ripe hazelnut, honeysuckle and candied mandarin peel, with a fine texture. I serve it at about ten degrees in a white wine glass so it can open.
table.sale: For a guest who loves Grand Cru Chardonnay, Femme de Champagne is a vintage wine of the Côte des Blancs, partly fermented in oak and long aged. May I open a bottle for you?
table.cuvee10: Femme de Champagne is Duval-Leroy's vintage prestige cuvée, mostly Grand Cru Chardonnay from the Côte des Blancs, first made in 1990.
table.cuvee20: Femme de Champagne is the vintage prestige cuvée of Duval-Leroy, mostly Grand Cru Chardonnay with a little Pinot Noir. A part is fermented in oak, which gives ripe hazelnut and honeysuckle with candied mandarin peel.

guests.q: Why is it called Femme de Champagne?
guests.a: It means woman of Champagne. The first vintage was 1990, and from 1991 the house was led by a woman, the widow of its late head.

guests.q: Is Femme de Champagne a Blanc de Blancs?
guests.a: Not quite. It is mostly Grand Cru Chardonnay, with a little Grand Cru Pinot Noir, so it is a blend in which Chardonnay leads by far.
At Vertus, in the south of the Côte des Blancs, below Épernay. Most houses on the class sheet stand at Reims or Épernay instead.

traps: The class sheet prints Cuvée Femme; the label reads Femme de Champagne, and the word cuvée is not in the name.
Femme de Champagne is Duval-Leroy's; La Grande Dame, the other cuvée named for a woman, is Veuve Clicquot's, of Reims.
Duval-Leroy is at Vertus in the Côte des Blancs, not at Reims or Épernay.
Femme de Champagne is not a pure Blanc de Blancs: a little Grand Cru Pinot Noir joins the Chardonnay.

sheet.label: Femme de Champagne
sheet.note: The sheet shortens the name and adds Cuvée. The label reads Femme de Champagne, woman of Champagne, and that full name is the one to say at the table.

questions.q: Which prestige cuvée on the class sheet is made by the family house of Vertus founded in 1859?
questions.exp: Femme de Champagne is Duval-Leroy's, the sheet's Cuvée Femme. La Grande Dame is Veuve Clicquot's, Belle Époque is Perrier-Jouët's and Amour de Deutz is the Blanc de Blancs of Deutz, of Aÿ.

questions.q: In which part of Champagne does Duval-Leroy stand?
opts: The Côte des Blancs, at Vertus
The Côte des Bar, at Urville
The Vallée de la Marne, at Aÿ
The Montagne de Reims, at Reims
questions.exp: Duval-Leroy is at Vertus, in the south of the Côte des Blancs. Urville in the Côte des Bar is Drappier's village, and Aÿ is home to Deutz, Gosset's old cellars and Bollinger.

questions.q: Which grape leads the blend of Femme de Champagne, by the house's pages?
questions.exp: Grand Cru Chardonnay from the Côte des Blancs leads by far, with a little Grand Cru Pinot Noir. Pinot Noir leads the house's Brut Réserve instead.

report: Not in the library and no flagships record: every fact rests on the house's pages, the Union des Maisons de Champagne or two secondary sources.
founded: the house and the union's house page give 1859; the union's chronology dates the two merchants' agreement to 1857, which the story tells as the agreement.
The founders' and the late head of the house's dates were not found, so none is named; his widow, who led the house from 1991, is living and is described, never named.
Femme's first vintage, 1990, rests on BKWine and Champagne Club; its release is dated 1996 by one profile and 1999 by another, so no release year is given; one merchant's 1911 is not taught.
The oak in the making rests on three critics' notes of three vintages; the house's own pages read do not give the share, the lees time or the dosage beside the 2002's Brut Nature.
cuvee.lees gives the sixteen years of the 2006 as one tasting note's account; a refuter should look for the house's sheet.
style.vessels is empty: the house does not state its vessels for the classic range on any page read. The style fields quote the Brut Réserve sheet of 2016, which may have moved since.
The first certified organic Brut and the High Environmental Value first are the house's own claims, told as its claims.
cuvee.bottle is empty: the shape's story rests on one trade article only.
kind.code: the letters NM were not read on a label; the union lists the house among its houses. A refuter should read a label.
cuvee.say spells the label's French; no source for the house's own saying was read.

changed: story and founded.what: Duval was a grower and maker of Vertus and Leroy a wine trader of Villers-Franqueux (Wikipedia, the Hameau Albert sheet), not two merchants; both now say a family of Vertus and a wine trading family.
story: the widow had married into the founding family, not descended from it by marriage.
story: the Clos des Bouveries is at Vertus; above the village had no source.

story and guests[2]: one of the few large houses based in the Côte des Blancs had no source and is cut; the guest's answer now says what the sheet itself shows, that most of its houses stand at Reims or Épernay.

cuvee.making: about a fifth of the 2002 aged in barrels of 220 litres, by the house's Femme de Champagne technical sheet, added beside the critics' notes; that sheet replaces the union's house page among the sources, the union's chronology standing.
open: The release of the 1990 Femme: one profile gives 1999, another 1996; still left out.
